header.title: Anthropic subscriptions outvalue OpenAI's, signaling differing lab unit economics

s01_bottom_line.text: SemiAnalysis's measurements find Anthropic's Claude subscription plans offer ~5x the API-equivalent value of OpenAI's at the mid-tier, and ~4x for Opus 5.5, after OpenAI halved its $200 plan value and cut limits to Fable-level across the board. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

The article implies that to model AI lab financials accurately, one must track subscription limits because they heavily affect margins and revenue per MW despite being a small revenue share, and that Anthropic currently crushes OpenAI on subscriber value. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

The value gap reflects divergent subsidy strategies rather than any disclosed profit metric for listed equities; it bears on private labs' unit economics and consumer goodwill, not directly on a public stock earnings line the article quantifies.

s03_transmission.text: Both labs heavily subsidize subscription plans; OpenAI chose to cut limits sharply while Anthropic reduces value only on premium models.
OpenAI halved $200 plan API-equivalent value and cut Sol pricing; Anthropic retains far higher per-dollar value across tiers. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
Subscription gross margins are far below API and depend on model mix and utilization (e.g. -369% to 6% for Opus 5.5, 1% to 80% for Fable 5.1).
Neither lab is publicly listed, so the article quantifies no listed-company earnings impact; relevance is to private valuations and competitive positioning.
